newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. council mulls request for meeting on Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: U.N. council mulls request for meeting on Jerusalem.

text.p: The Security Council held inconclusive consultations on Thursday on an Arab group's request for a meeting to demand that Israel halt a controversial construction project in Arab East Jerusalem.
Council members' Middle East experts were to consult further later in the day.

At issue is the start of work by Israel on Tuesday on 6,500 homes for Jews on a hill between Jerusalem and Bethlehem that Israel captured during the 1967 Middle East war. The site is called Jabal Abu Ghneim by Palestinians and Har Homa by Israelis.

A resolution drafted by the 22-member Arab group would demand that Israel "immediately cease construction of the Jabal Abu Ghneim settlement in East Jerusalem, as well as all other Israeli settlement activities in the occupied territories."
Council sources said the United States, which vetoed a resolution on March 7 calling on Israel to abandon plans for the project, was almost certain to veto another such draft.

Although critical of Israel's action, the United States says the United Nations is not the appropriate forum for dealing with differences that should be settled directly between the Palestinians and Israel.

But council sources said the United States was willing to agree to a statement, to be read out by the council president, calling for a halt to the Israeli construction work and stressing the need to proceed with the Middle East peace process.

The ongoing consultations were expected to focus on whether the Arab group, represented in the council by Egypt, would agree to a presidential statement, even though it carries less weight than a resolution, or whether the group would insist on pressing its resolution to a vote, with the strong likelihood of a veto.

After the March 7 U.S. veto in the Security Council, the Arab group transferred the issue to the General Assembly, where a similar resolution was adopted March 13 by a vote of 130 to 2, with two abstentions. The United States and Israel cast the only negative votes in the Assembly, whose resolutions are not binding.
